title: [bug] remote tar size cap overflows on a crafted entry

description: strspc-CLI#286 is blocked on this. Contract: strspc-rules docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-standards-as-realms-design.md, section Coverage. The src/coverage package must: resolve the Standard Realm a Standard Reference links to through realm (STDREF-017), a dependency of the realm tree; build its clause list from the live rules' clause values (STDRLM-005/007/014), narrowed to profile when one is set (STDREF-020), counting a clause split across rules once; read the manifest's exclusion Realm Notes, each giving the status excluded (STDREF-022), and treat a clause that is none of covered, mapped, lapsed or excluded as unmapped (STDREF-023); compute the entity figure covered / (list - excluded) (STDREF-024) and the realm figure across the tree (STDREF-025), undefined when the divisor is 0 (STDREF-028), with no figure for derived_from (STDREF-026). Shares the linked-Standard-Realm loading and clause list with 18c.2 (cross-realm lint), so build that once and use it in both. Related: k7e (coverage Compare, clauses qualified by realm). Reuse entity.IsLiveStandardRule and entity.NoteTypeExclusion from #310/#311.
notes: Branch feat/linked-coverage. Acceptance: CLI can drop message parsing (and its own scope walk) after bumping manager; RL031 output unchanged.

title: Supersede MOD-002 to list the EC (evalcache) diagnostic prefix

A Published/Implemented body is final, so use 'strspc rule supersede MOD-002 --dir rules' with the seven-prefix wording, then promote the successor D→P→I (the test already enforces it).
notes: Needs three PRs, one per state change, because rule-diff forbids skipping states: (1) strspc rule supersede MOD-002 --dir rules adds the successor (MOD-007 (MOD-006 is taken)) in D with all seven prefixes (RL, RD, RM, RR, RSV, RE, EC) and supersedes: MOD-002 (RD004: new rules start in D); (2) strspc rule promote D->P (RD003: D->I in one diff is a skip); (3) promote P->I and retire MOD-002 I->R in the same PR (RD006 warns otherwise). Each PR touches only rules/MOD.json; no Go changes, since ownedPrefix in src/result/codes_lifecycle_test.go already maps src/evalcache to EC. A clarification note is not enough: notes must not modify the rule (SPEC 2.5).
